verdict_basis: The documented P04I non-admission is LAWFUL and SAFE, and this reviewer could not break it. (1) Lawfulness: dossier 05 line 5 admits a receiver change ONLY on material measured result-put/commit backpressure; the P04I receipts take the explicit not_admitted branch; the P04R task text ('Accept or reject candidate, or verify documented non-admission') makes verification a lawful completion. (2) Every decision-run number re-derived independently: my own extraction of the raw m_w4t phase events (own merge/union/interval code, no implementer probe reused) reproduces result_recv 32/0.000359s, dispatch 32/0.000465s, per-row commit max 0.222946s, commit_publish max 0.206187s/sum 4.018985s, commit_staged_verify sum 0.690765s, row-31 put 1.850811s at cpu/wall 0.9824, other-31-puts 0.027301s, union busy 6.043636s of span 25.574542s (idle 0.7637), tail after last recv 0.835738s, pool_close 0.713726s - all matching receiver_admission.json to the printed precision. (3) Backpressure absence re-derived from intervals, not spans: the coordinator's recv blocking is invisible to the result_recv span by construction (runtime.py:1159 recv sits OUTSIDE the span; design-01 comment at runtime.py:1162-1166), so I checked the real criteria: worker puts never block (all 31 non-31 puts are 0.0003-0.0087s; row 31 is main-thread CPU-bound, see reviewer_added_evidence), worst per-row commit 0.2229s < my corrected mean inter-arrival 0.3387s (the receipt's ~0.7s is imprecise but the criterion holds a fortiori at the true margin 1.5x; max single gap 2.807s >> max commit), zero overlap between the row-31 put span and any other put (no SimpleQueue write-lock stall), and workers idle in inbox_get 0.77-3.46s each (unsaturated). No monotone outbox growth is possible: _pending_bound (runtime.py:1493-1496) caps outstanding results at workers+queue_depth, pinned by the passing test_bounded_pending_dispatch. (4) Oversized-state safety - the key adversarial question - answered NO latent gap: dossier 05's credits-before-dispatch law is scoped to the NEW receiver's bounded ready map ('First schedule: one receiver, one commit owner'), and the same dossier explicitly permits 'the original route' for unknown response bounds; on that original route oversized state is handled at BOTH boundaries by committed, currently passing code: dispatch-side probe-pickle _job_transport_failure (runtime.py:1470-1480, called at 1059 before pool.dispatch) fails the row loudly through the normal earliest-failure path, and worker-side _transport_safe (worker.py:553-581) degrades an untransportable RESULT in two loud stages instead of killing a feeder thread; the outbox is a synchronous ctx.SimpleQueue (_ResultChannel, runtime.py:324-357) whose put pickles and writes under a lock before returning, so death after put cannot lose a completed result - pinned by test_result_channel_put_is_synchronous_across_abrupt_death (asserts the delivered payload AND exitcode==1) which I re-ran green. (5) Commit ownership and cancellation/resume semantics: exactly one commit owner (single _commit_worker_row call site at runtime.py:1133 inside the coordinator loop); git diff vs the P00-era tree e7c9eda for runtime.py shows the staged_verify -> publish -> state_apply -> capture_write -> outcome -> journal -> prefix_check statements preserved VERBATIM inside new observation spans (the only +/- lines touching _verify_staged/_publish_staged are re-indentation), and the worker-death drain (runtime.py:1075-1094), _cancel/_close/pool teardown, and recv restructure are behavior-preserving; tests/tenx islands I ran green: transport+cancellation 12 passed, overlap 3 passed, checkpoint/resume 12 passed. (6) Fault matrix soundness: the 7 conditions are the right axes for dossier 05; the 5 'absent' rows are measured and independently reproduced by this review; 'measured_not_backpressure' (row-31 put) is replicated 4/4 with exact max-put facts in all four P01 runs; 'not_applicable_no_receiver' is correct - TEST_MATRIX RX01-RX05 attach to a receiver implementation that does not exist, and the ORIGINAL-route-relevant parts of RX02 (worker death during put, oversized result transport) are already covered by the passing committed tests above. Findings: 0 blocking; 5 non-blocking evidence-hygiene defects/observations in the committed receipt wording/derived numbers (NR-1 inverted nesting description, NR-2 mis-composed p01 other-put sums, NR-3 a false '<0.1s in every run' claim for load_w4, NR-4 imprecise inter-arrival figure, NR-5 unexercised full-pipe stall) - none changes the measured basis or the decision.

reviewer_added_evidence.row31_put_attribution_sharpened: The receipt's attribution_bound claims the 1.85s CPU 'is NOT further attributed (pickle-vs-gc-vs-feeder-marshal is not further separated)'. The raw events DO further separate it: the row-31 result_put span records thread_cpu delta 1.818187s vs process_cpu delta 1.818193s - essentially ALL the CPU burned in the worker's MAIN thread, which is the thread executing _transport_safe's pickle.dumps probe and SimpleQueue.put's synchronous pickle+write. A SimpleQueue has no feeder thread at all, and a blocked main thread would show thread_cpu << process_cpu.
